title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 134 (Discharge of surety by release or discharge of principal debtor)

content.overview: Section 134 provides that the surety is discharged by any contract between the creditor and the principal debtor by which the principal debtor is released, or by any act or omission of the creditor the legal consequence of which is the discharge of the principal debtor. The statutory illustrations cover release by composition with creditors and discharge by the creditor's act preventing performance.
content.glance: Release or legal discharge of the principal debtor by the creditor discharges the surety.
content.study: The surety is discharged by any contract between the creditor and the principal debtor by which the principal debtor is released, or by any act or omission of the creditor the legal consequence of which is the discharge of the principal debtor. Identify the release or the act/omission and its legal effect of discharging the principal debtor. Current-law framing: the discharge of the surety follows the legal discharge of the principal debtor.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The surety is discharged by any contract between the creditor and the principal debtor by which the principal debtor is released, or by any act or omission of the creditor the legal consequence of which is the discharge of the principal debtor.

sections.heading: Release by contract
sections.body: A contract that releases the principal debtor discharges the surety.

sections.heading: Act or omission
sections.body: An act or omission of the creditor whose legal consequence is discharge of the principal debtor also discharges the surety.

examples.title: Release by composition
examples.body: A guarantees goods supplied by C to B. B later assigns property to creditors including C in consideration of release. A is discharged.

examples.title: Act preventing performance
examples.body: C guarantees A's performance of growing indigo for B. B diverts water necessary for the crop, preventing performance. C is discharged.

hypotheticals.question: The creditor releases the principal debtor by agreement without the surety's assent. Is the surety discharged?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 134 provides that release of the principal debtor by contract discharges the surety.

illustrations: Section 134 Illustration (a): release by composition with creditors discharges the surety.
Section 134 Illustration (b): creditor's act preventing performance discharges the surety.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 134 discharges the surety when the principal debtor is released by contract with the creditor, or when an act or omission of the creditor has the legal consequence of discharging the principal debtor. The illustrations confirm discharge on composition-release and on an act that prevents performance. Mere forbearance is addressed separately in Section 137.
examples: Composition releasing the principal debtor discharges the surety.
Creditor's act preventing the principal debtor's performance discharges the surety.
distinctions: Section 134 concerns release or legal discharge of the principal debtor; Section 137 provides that mere forbearance to sue does not discharge the surety.
